about.greeting: I am a fullstack developer with a strong bias toward quality and data. I started out reading data on a market intelligence team, learned how production breaks while working in support, and since 2022 I have been building software from the database to the interface. The same thread runs through all three phases: understand the problem before picking the tool.
about.professionalDescription: Today I work fullstack at Stech, on internal and client products, with TypeScript, React, NestJS and Prisma over MySQL, all containerised. Before that: Java and Spring Boot at Persys, the longest tenure of my career; conversion-focused frontend at Make; and test engineering at Outlier, evaluating language models across voice, vision and text. For just over a year I also taught Excel, Power BI and generative AI at Cebrac — teaching is what forces you to actually understand something.
about.expertiseDescription: What I bring to a team is judgement, not a stack list. Auditing and fixing vulnerabilities in a financial suite before they become an incident. Turning business rules into traceable parameters instead of leaving them hardcoded. Treating Core Web Vitals as a requirement rather than decoration — that is the bar behind more than a hundred landing pages. And automating where it reduces risk: TaskForge, which orchestrates agents in parallel, cut 70% to 90% of the engineering LLM bill. When a subject is complex, explaining it is part of the delivery.

taskforge.title: TaskForge
taskforge.description: Parallel agent orchestrator. Turns a request into a task graph, isolates each task in its own worktree and runs them in waves, with human review and merge at the end. Cut 70% to 90% of the engineering LLM bill.

stechclub.title: StechClub
stechclub.description: Stech's education portal: a React SPA behind company SSO, with a NestJS API over Prisma. Video and thumbnails live in S3 and are served through signed links generated by the API, never exposing the bucket key. The application funnel uses a fit quiz with a minimum score and distinct replies for passing and failing candidates.

barbearia_app.title: Barbershop App
barbearia_app.description: Discovery and booking PWA for barbershops, with map, live schedule and separate owner and customer roles. Double-booking is prevented by a database constraint rather than an application check.

pasta_la_vista.title: Pasta la Vista
pasta_la_vista.description: Delivery app with menu, cart, orders and payment. Clean Architecture on the backend, with storage split across PostgreSQL, MongoDB and Redis according to data shape.

buscajogos.title: BuscaJogos+
buscajogos.description: Final-year project: a price comparison tool for digital games, with wishlist and sale alerts. Database, Go API and frontend split into containers, built from real user problem research.

kitbuilder.title: KitBuilder / S.A.G.A.
kitbuilder.description: Electronic parts inventory control in a layered architecture, with repositories, versioned migrations, spreadsheet import and a test suite. Final project for the Multiplatform Software Development degree at Fatec Mauá, published in the Centro Paula Souza institutional repository.

youtcatcher.title: YoutCatcher
youtcatcher.description: Desktop video downloader with a GUI, persistent history and strict MVC. Over 80% test coverage and structured logging, in a project that could have been a throwaway script.

sudoku_solver.title: Sudoku Solver
sudoku_solver.description: Solves a Sudoku from a photo: image pre-processing, grid detection, digit OCR, a backtracking solver in C and the answer overlaid back onto the original picture.

asurapadel.title: AsuraPadel
asurapadel.description: Padel court management across two applications: an Angular frontend and a C# API deployed on Azure. The interesting part is performance — response times degraded once the API moved to a test server, and the fix combined caching, endpoint redesign, batched pagination, payload reduction and client-side work. Reported average response time went from 800 ms to 220 ms.

portal_agente_ia.title: AI agent operations portal
portal_agente_ia.description: Portal for running and auditing an AI-driven WhatsApp support channel. The product is not the agent: it is the interface that lets a non-technical person test, follow and correct it. It brought prompt versioning with rollback and a separate webhook isolating sandbox traffic from real traffic — quality control applied to a non-deterministic system. Client under confidentiality: no name, repository or screenshot.

bubble_box_lavanderia.title: Bubble Box
bubble_box_lavanderia.description: Landing page for a self-service laundry franchise, covering store formats, unit search and lead capture as the stated goal. Core Web Vitals was an acceptance criterion, not a later refinement.

jarbas.title: Jarbas
jarbas.description: A second-brain assistant over a Markdown vault, with a CLI and a desktop interface. Its core is an action gate: every agent write passes through a checkpoint that validates the plan before touching a file, so automation cannot corrupt the knowledge base it is meant to maintain.

quinto_selo.title: Quinto Selo
quinto_selo.description: Online co-op 2D roguelite built in Godot 4, themed around the four horsemen. The hard part is not combat: it is the netcode and the two-body death rule, both closed out with headless verification before becoming playable.

financeos.title: FinanceOS
financeos.description: Personal finance management in a Turborepo monorepo, with Prisma for persistence, Redis for the hot paths and per-workspace stores.

zoologic.title: Zoologic
zoologic.description: Zoo management split into two sub-projects: a PHP 8 API written against SOLID with a real PHPUnit suite, and a Next.js frontend. The point was proving that modern PHP takes architecture and serious testing.

repo_explorer_angular.title: Repo Explorer
repo_explorer_angular.description: A GitHub repository explorer built in Angular with signals, delivered as a take-home test for a senior role. CI was green on submission.

instagram_analyzer.title: Instagram Analyzer
instagram_analyzer.description: Desktop app that reads Instagram's JSON export and surfaces who does not follow back, with indicators and live search. Fully local — the file never leaves the machine.

pokedex.title: Pokédex
pokedex.description: Mobile exploration app with local SQLite persistence and Reanimated animations, built to work offline after the first load.

javafx_pokemon.title: JavaFX Pokémon
javafx_pokemon.description: JavaFX desktop application with Maven and MVC separation — a Java architecture exercise, built to practise layering rather than just screens.

calc_financeira.description: Financial mathematics calculator in plain Python, with no external dependencies — interest, amortisation and series, with the logic kept in a single file.

aquila_e_evelyn.title: Aquila & Evelyn
aquila_e_evelyn.description: A digital wedding invitation reworked as a sanitized public showcase: responsive static page, custom visual identity, CSS animation and vanilla JavaScript interactions, with event details and personal content removed.

presente_para_daniela.title: Gift for Daniela
presente_para_daniela.description: A narrative Next.js experience with gothic art direction, horizontal scrolling, microinteractions and GSAP animation. The public edition preserves the design and engineering while removing personal photos, drawings, dates, music and messages.

suite_financeira_b2b.title: B2B financial suite
suite_financeira_b2b.description: Financial operations suite across three repositories: a Django backend with DRF, JWT and async tasks; a Vue 3 interface with an in-house design system; and PySpark pipelines feeding silver and gold layers. Kafka wires the domains together with a topic per subject, consumers with error handling and a DLQ, and per-environment consumer deployments. AWS shows up as S3 with presigned URLs, SQS and Secrets Manager — not just storage. Vulnerability remediation put pip-audit inside the CI build job. Client under confidentiality: no name, repository or screenshot.

portal_remuneracao_frota.title: Payroll and fleet portal
portal_remuneracao_frota.description: Internal portal for monthly payroll closing, fleet mileage, base records and reports, built on Lumen and React with TypeScript. The case is measurement: the closing screen fired 354 queries per load and ten of the eleven domain tables had no index at all, with 293 thousand rows in full scan. Seven indexes derived from the measured predicates took the screen from 4,271 ms to 354 ms with a byte-identical response; the remaining N+1 was mapped at 316 of the 354 queries. It also produced deploy-hygiene fixes: a config file pointing at localhost kept out of the commit, and a backup .env the gitignore did not cover. Client under confidentiality: no name, repository or screenshot.

servidor_llm_local.title: Self-hosted LLM server
servidor_llm_local.description: Internal server turned into a local model host and file store. Ubuntu 24.04 on bare metal, Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and the GPU visible inside the container; Ollama serving an 8B model over the local API. Remote access through Tailscale rather than an internet-facing port, and authenticated Samba shares with no guest access. Sizing was stated alongside the delivery: this hardware profile serves RAG and quantised 7B/8B models, not heavy multi-user inference.

payroll.context: The monthly closing screen fired 354 queries per load, including full scans over 293 thousand rows.
payroll.constraint: Ten of the eleven domain tables had no index, while the response had to remain byte-identical.
payroll.decision: Create seven indexes derived from the measured predicates and map the remaining N+1.
payroll.evidence: The response was compared byte-for-byte after the change; the remaining N+1 was identified in 316 of the 354 queries.
payroll.impact: Screen time dropped from 4,271 ms to 354 ms.
